job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today at school, we had a discussion about our country's diversity. My friend Rohan, who speaks Punjabi at home, was teased by some boys because they thought people who speak different languages are less intelligent. I felt sad because I know that speaking a different language does not make someone unequal. Later, our teacher explained that we often form fixed ideas about groups, like assuming all people from a certain region are lazy. She called these stereotypes and said they prevent us from seeing each person as a unique individual. She also told us that prejudice is not just having a strong opinion; it is judging others negatively before even knowing them. We learned that our Constitution guarantees equality for everyone, regardless of their background or caste. It was an eye-opening day. I realized that diversity is not a problem to be solved, but a strength that makes India special. We must respect everyone's differences instead of discriminating against them. I want to make sure I never judge someone based on these unfair labels again. It is important to treat every classmate with the same kindness and respect, no matter where they come from or what language they speak.

items.evidence: I felt sad because I know that speaking a different language does not make someone unequal.
items.q: A new classmate speaks only Tamil at home. What does this tell you about her worth?
options: She is equal to everyone else in class
She is less clever than Hindi speakers
She must be shy like all Tamil speakers
She should sit only with Tamil speakers
items.explain: Speaking a different language does not make someone unequal, so she is equal to everyone.

wrong.why: thinks a different language makes someone unequal
thinks everyone in a group has the same personality
thinks different groups should stay apart

items.evidence: She called these stereotypes and said they prevent us from seeing each person as a unique individual.
items.q: Why did the teacher say stereotypes are a problem?
options: They make us ignore what each person is like
They are a problem only when they insult people
They are mostly true but rude to say aloud
They make groups live apart and never mix
items.explain: Stereotypes stop us from seeing each person as a unique individual.

wrong.why: thinks a stereotype is only a problem when insulting
thinks stereotypes are true because many say them
mixes up stereotypes with groups living separately

items.evidence: She also told us that prejudice is not just having a strong opinion; it is judging others negatively before even knowing them.
items.q: Meena decides a new boy is rude before she has spoken to him. What is this?
options: Prejudice, because she judges him too early
A strong opinion, which is her fair right
A stereotype, because it is an insult
Diversity, because he is different from her
items.explain: Prejudice is judging others negatively before even knowing them, not just a strong opinion.

wrong.why: thinks prejudice is just a strong opinion
thinks any insult is a stereotype, though this is about one person
picks a nearby key word from the passage

items.evidence: We learned that our Constitution guarantees equality for everyone, regardless of their background or caste.
items.q: A school refuses to admit a girl because of her caste. What does our Constitution say?
options: Every person has equal rights whatever their caste
Each caste may run its own separate schools
Only differences of religion are protected by it
Equal rights apply only to well-educated people
items.explain: The Constitution guarantees equality for everyone, regardless of background or caste, so refusing her is wrong.

wrong.why: thinks groups should be kept separate
links unequal treatment to being uneducated

items.evidence: I realized that diversity is not a problem to be solved, but a strength that makes India special.
items.q: By the end of the day, what did the writer believe about India's many differences?
options: India's differences are a valuable strength
India's differences are a problem to solve
India's differences are fine if groups stay apart
India's differences are only about religion
items.explain: The writer realised diversity is not a problem but a strength that makes India special.

wrong.why: thinks diversity means groups living separately
thinks diversity in India means only religion
